newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China-HK Photo sees sales fall Apr-Sept.
newsitem.headline: China-HK Photo sees sales fall Apr-Sept.

text.p: China-Hongkong Photo Products Holdings Ltd said on Friday it expected a year-on-year fall in turnover in the six months to September 30.
High inventory levels held by distributors, changes in its distribution system and recent floods in southern and central China had affected sales in China, it said in a statement.
"This will lead to a decrease in turnover for the first half of the 1996/97 financial year, compared with the same period in the previous year," said chairman Dennis Sun.
The firm, which distributes Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd products in Hong Kong, Macau and China, did not give figures.

Its policy to reduce the inventory held by importers, which would enable the group to maintain greater control over sales and even out sales fluctuations, led to a reduction in sales in April and May, the statement said.

The firm, which distributes in China through other distributors and its joint ventures, added its joint ventures accounted for 35 percent of total sales, up from the previous 26 percent, amid a move towards a more localised distribution system.

But joint venture sales were booked as inter-company transactions and not as "sales" on the profit/loss account until they were sold on to a third party, whereas sales through distributors were booked straightaway, the statement said.

"We expect this to be a transitional stage as we move towards a more localised distribution system that, in the long term, will allow us to maintain more consistent sales and general higher margins. The underlying growth in the market for film products in China is still very healthy," Sun said.
China-Hongkong Photo claimed a share of about 50 percent of the roll film market in China and Hong Kong.
